concept.name: Wyckoff Phase A
concept.definition: The first phase of a Wyckoff trading range, marking the stopping of the prior trend. In accumulation it contains preliminary support, the selling climax, the automatic rally, and secondary tests; in distribution it contains preliminary supply, the buying climax, the automatic reaction, and secondary tests.
concept.intuition: The moment the old trend finally runs out of gas — panic at bottoms, euphoria at tops — and the sideways battle begins.
concept.mechanics: Phase A transfers large volumes of shares between the public and professional interests through climactic price and volume action. The highs and lows formed during Phase A (climax and automatic move) set the boundaries of the trading range used in all subsequent analysis.
concept.failure_modes: Trends can stop without climactic action, making Phase A hard to recognize; and climactic action can be followed by trend continuation rather than a range, so Phase A labeling is provisional until a range develops.
concept.misconceptions: Phase A does not require a dramatic climax — Wyckoff notes trends can end quietly with decreasing spread and volume — and a climax alone does not guarantee a reversal.
concept.example: A year-long slide ends with a high-volume support day (PS), a panic flush (SC), a sharp bounce (AR), and a quiet retest (ST); the analyst marks these four events as Phase A and draws range boundaries at the AR high and SC low.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
